results.summary:
The `copilot-cli` profile is in, generated from templates and wired end to end.

**1. Built-in `copilot-cli` profile** (`src/board.js`): `copilot -p {prompt} --agent kanban-worker --allow-tool 'shell(...)' ×N --deny-tool 'shell(git push --force*)' [--model M]`, `heartbeat: "auto"`, `max_in_progress: 1` (Copilot Free's credit pool is small). Copilot repeats `--allow-tool` per pattern instead of taking a list, so `expandLaunch` (dispatch.js) grew an `--allow-tool={allowed_tools}` token that emits one flag pair per entry. The allowlist is now ONE list of shell patterns (`SHELL_TOOLS`) rendered into both `Bash(...)` for Claude and `shell(...)` for Copilot, so the two cannot drift apart.

**2. A dispatcher-made worktree.** A profile can declare `workspace: "worktree"`; `spawnWorker` then calls the new `ensureWorktree(root, name)` in board.js (`git worktree add .claude/worktrees/kb-<n>-<k> -b kb-<n>-<k>`, reuses an existing checkout, falls back to checking out a branch an earlier attempt left behind) and runs the worker with that as its cwd. Same directory Claude Code uses, so `hkb gc` already sweeps them. `attempt.wt` is now recorded for process workers too, not only background ones.

**3. `hkb init --harness copilot`** writes `.github/agents/kanban-worker.agent.md` and `.github/hooks/kanban.json` from `templates/copilot/`. The agent body is spliced out of the packaged `skills/kanban/SKILL.md` (only the skill-relative `references/protocol.md` link is rewritten), so the protocol text lives in exactly one place; both files are generated and re-running init rewrites them. `--harness copilot` on its own also brings the `copilot-cli` profile and replaces the `claude` default (`resolveProfiles` in init.js — pure, tested); naming `--profiles` too keeps both.

`hkb hook stop` now serves both harnesses: `normalizeHookInput` (model.js) folds Copilot's camelCase `agentStop` payload onto Claude's snake_case, and `{"decision":"block","reason":…}` is what both read back. `src/hook.js` carries the full comparison table — event name, config file, stdin spelling, stdout, and why it is `agentStop` and not `sessionEnd`.

Also: `hkb doctor` warns when the `copilot-cli` profile is configured but the generated files are missing (without them `--agent kanban-worker` resolves to nothing and no hook enforces the terminal verb); `init` now gitignores `.claude/worktrees/` and `.kanban/sessions/`, which hkb writes but did not ignore.

## Caveat for the next worker — the docs check did not happen

The task asked to verify flag names against docs.github.com. **This worker had no web access** (WebFetch, WebSearch and outbound shell were all denied by the permission mode) and `copilot` is not installed on this host, so `copilot --help` was not available either. The flags and the hook-config schema follow `docs/EVALUATION.md`, which was written from those docs.

Two things need a networked check before the profile is used for real. Both are isolated so a correction is a one-line edit:

- **(a)** `-p`, `--agent`, `--allow-tool`, `--deny-tool`, `--model`, and whether `shell(hkb *)` accepts a wildcard — all in the `copilot-cli` `launch` array in `src/board.js`. The wildcard is the assumption to check first; if it is not supported the allowlist needs exact commands.
- **(b)** The hook config shape in `templates/copilot/hooks.json` (Claude-style `hooks.<event>[].hooks[]` nesting, event name `agentStop`). Nothing in `src/` parses it, so correcting the template is enough.

Flags I was less confident about (`--no-color`, `--log-level`) were deliberately left out so an unknown flag cannot make every attempt fail at launch, and the generated agent's frontmatter is kept to `name` + `description` for the same reason. PR #32 spells all of this out for the reviewer.

## Why `request-review` and not `complete`

Two reasons, and they point the same way. Substantively: the two unverified assumptions above need someone with a browser to check them against docs.github.com before this counts as done — which is what this verb is for. Mechanically: `hkb complete` could not be run from this attempt at all. The harness's worktree-isolation guard matches the bare token `complete` in any command line and refuses it ("this command runs a string through complete, which can't be verified to stay inside the worktree"), including `hkb complete --help` and `node bin/hkb.js complete …`. `heartbeat` and `request-review` pass the same guard. Worth fixing in the harness; it makes `complete` unreachable for any worker running in an isolated worktree.
